documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Postpartum f/u, 8 weeks after cesarean + BTL (12/16), which was complicated by hemorrhage and 2 u PRBC.

S: Still very tired and foggy; the baby is up twice a night but she says it's more than that. Lightheaded on standing most days. No milk ever came in - bottle-feeding. No bleeding since the surgery. Appetite meh. Incision healed. Husband is doing nights on weekends. Endocrinology appointment is 6/23, on their cancellation list. HRT still off since REI stopped it last January; would rather wait for endocrinology's advice.

Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 daily, vitamin D3, desmopressin PRN.

O: BP 98/62, vitals otherwise as recorded. Thin, pale. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen: low transverse scar well healed, nontender. No edema. PHQ-9 6 - mostly tiredness and concentration items; no thoughts of self-harm.

A/P:
1. Fatigue and orthostatic symptoms after second PPH - endocrinology pending for pituitary evaluation. Return or ED for vomiting, confusion, fainting.
2. Iron deficiency anemia after blood loss - CBC, iron studies today; continue oral iron.
3. S/p cesarean and tubal ligation - added to history. Postpartum hemorrhage resolved.
4. Mood - PHQ-9 6, will rescreen.
Follow-up after the endocrinology visit.

events.reason: Amenorrhea and failed lactation after second delivery

conditions.label: Hypopituitarism
conditions.note: Postpartum pituitary insufficiency (Sheehan syndrome) with secondary adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 2026-06-23
Referred by: primary care

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Klein, 35, whom our group last followed years ago for her Kallmann syndrome. She delivered her second child by cesarean six months ago; that delivery was complicated by hemorrhage and transfusion, as was her first in 2023 (uterine inversion, then retained placenta). Since December she has not had a period and never produced milk. She is tired all the time and has noticed thinning of her pubic and axillary hair. Her estradiol/norethindrone has been off since January 2025 for fertility treatment.

Other history: type 1 von Willebrand disease; iron deficiency anemia; tubal ligation at the cesarean. Medications: ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, desmopressin nasal as needed. Allergy: latex.

Exam: BP 90/60. BMI 19. Pale. No galactorrhea on breast exam.

Labs this morning (08:05): sodium 130, potassium 5.2, calcium 9.0; cortisol 3 mcg/dL; TSH 0.5 with free T4 0.8; prolactin 5.

Assessment: hypopituitarism following postpartum hemorrhage (Sheehan syndrome), with secondary adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism. Low prolactin explains the failed lactation. The underlying Kallmann syndrome means her gonadotropin deficiency predates this.

Plan:
1. Hydrocortisone 10 mg on waking and 5 mg at about 2 PM, started today. Sick-day rules reviewed: double the doses for fever or illness, and seek care for vomiting. A medical alert ID and an emergency steroid letter given.
2. Levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, starting four days after the hydrocortisone. Dose by free T4, not TSH.
3. Resume ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 5 mcg/1 mg daily for estrogen replacement.
4. Desmopressin only for bleeding; with her low sodium, limit fluids that day.
5. Labs and visit here in 6 weeks.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endocrinology (letter 6/23 reviewed).

S: Endocrinology diagnosed postpartum hypopituitarism - Sheehan's - with secondary adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism. Started hydrocortisone 10 mg on waking / 5 mg early afternoon on 6/23; levothyroxine 50 mcg began 6/27; back on her estradiol/norethindrone. After a week she already feels steadier on her feet and a bit less flat in the afternoons. No vomiting, no fevers. Has her alert bracelet ordered and the emergency letter in her bag.

Meds: hydrocortisone 10 mg AM / 5 mg PM, levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 5 mcg/1 mg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU, desmopressin nasal PRN.

O: BP 94/62. Weight 51.7 kg. Thin, pale. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema. PHQ-2 1.

A/P:
1. Hypopituitarism after postpartum hemorrhage - added to problem list; replacement per endocrinology. Reviewed sick-day doubling and when to go to the ED. Flagged chart: stress-dose steroids for any procedure or acute illness.
2. Hyponatremia - expect improvement on hydrocortisone; endocrinology rechecks in 6 weeks.
3. Kallmann syndrome - HRT resumed.
4. Iron deficiency - continue iron.
5. vWD - desmopressin sparingly, fluids limited that day.
RTC September.

documents.title: Two weeks in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just a note - two weeks on the hydrocortisone and I'm noticeably better. I took the stairs at work today without having to stop. My husband says I'm talking more. The bracelet came. Thank you.

documents.title: RE: Two weeks in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is so good to hear. Keep everything as endocrinology set it, and remember to double the hydrocortisone if you get sick. See you in September.
